metadata.title: Localizing Changes in High-Dimensional Regression Models

extraction_notes.note: Custom 'Model' environment (type null); typed as assumption since it posits the data-generating model, though it also introduces K, eta_k and Sigma (could be a definition).

The proof-sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal on sketch proofs, but rigor is not allowed on proof nodes; left rigor off. PP2 is the main proves edge for Proposition 5, which has no proof of its own besides Lemmas 12-15 (named cases), so only its edge to Proposition 6 is alternative.

nodes.name: Change point linear regression model
nodes.statement:
Let the data  $\{(x_t, y_t)\}_{t = 1}^n \subset \mathbb{R}^p \times \mathbb{R}$ satisfy the model
		\[
			y_t = x_t^\top \beta_t^* + \varepsilon_t, \quad t =1, \ldots, n
		\]
		where $\{\beta_t^*\}_{t = 1}^n \subset \mathbb{R}^p$ is the unknown coefficient vector, $\{x_t\}_{t = 1}^n$ are independent and identically distributed mean-zero sub-Gaussian random  vectors with $\mathbb{E}(x_t x_t^{\top}) = \Sigma$,  and $\{\varepsilon_t\}_{t = 1}^n$ are independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian random variables with sub-Gaussian parameter bounded by $\sigma_{\varepsilon}^2$ and independent of $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^n$. 
	In addition, there exists a sequence of change points $1 = \eta_0 < \eta_1 < 
	\ldots < \eta_{K+1} = n$ such that $\beta_t^* \neq \beta_{t - 1}^*$, if and only if $t \in \{\eta_k\}_{k = 1}^K$.
nodes.statement_short: Linear regression $y_t = x_t^\top\beta_t^* + \varepsilon_t$ with sub-Gaussian design and noise, and coefficients piecewise constant with $K$ change points $\eta_k$.
nodes.label: assume:change point regression model

nodes.name: Consistent change point estimators
nodes.statement:
That is, we seek \emph{consistent} estimators $\{\hat{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\widehat{K}}$, such that, as the sample size $n$ grows unbounded, it holds with probability tending to 1 that 
	\[
		\widehat{K} = K \quad \mbox{and} \quad \epsilon = \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K} |\widehat \eta_k -\eta_k|  = o(\Delta),
	\]
	where $\Delta = \min_{k=1,\ldots,K_1} \eta_k - \eta_{k-1}$ is the minimal spacing between consecutive change-points.
nodes.statement_short: Estimators are consistent if $\widehat K = K$ and the maximal localization error $\epsilon$ is $o(\Delta)$ with probability tending to 1.

nodes.name: Localization error rate
nodes.statement: We refer to the quantity $\epsilon$ as the {\it localization error rate}.

nodes.name: Cardinality notation
nodes.statement: For any set $S$, $|S|$ denotes its cardinality.

nodes.name: Vector norms and coordinates
nodes.statement: For any vector $v$, let $\|v\|_2$, $\|v\|_1$, $\|v\|_0$ and $\|v\|_{\infty}$ be its $\ell_2$-, $\ell_1$-, $\ell_0$- and entry-wise maximum norms, respectively; and let $v(j)$ be the $j$th coordinate of $v$.

nodes.name: Extreme eigenvalues
nodes.statement: For any square matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, let $\Lambda_{\min}(A)$ and $ \Lambda_{\max}(A)$ be the smallest and largest eigenvalues of matrix $A$, respectively.

nodes.name: Integer intervals
nodes.statement: For any pair of integers $s, e \in \{0, 1, \ldots, n\}$ with $s < e$, we let $(s, e] = \{s + 1, \ldots, e\}$ and $[s, e] = \{s , \ldots, e\}$ be the corresponding integer intervals.

nodes.name: Integer interval partition
Minimal partition problem
nodes.statement:
For a positive tuning parameter $\gamma > 0$, let 
	\begin{equation} \widehat{\mathcal{P}} \in arg\,min_{\mathcal{P}} \left\{\sum_{I \in \mathcal{P}} \mathcal{L}(I) + \gamma |\mathcal{P}|\right\}, 
	\end{equation}
	where $\mathcal{L}(\cdot)$ is an appropriate loss function to be specified below, $|\mathcal{P}|$ is the cardinality of $\mathcal{P}$ and the minimization is taken over all possible interval partitions of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Penalized minimal partition: choose the interval partition minimizing total segment loss plus $\gamma$ times the number of intervals.

nodes.name: Penalized partition objective
nodes.statement: \widehat{\mathcal{P}} \in arg\,min_{\mathcal{P}} \left\{\sum_{I \in \mathcal{P}} \mathcal{L}(I) + \gamma |\mathcal{P}|\right\},
nodes.label: eq-wide-p

nodes.name: Change point estimator from optimal partition
nodes.statement: The change point estimator resulting from the solution to \eqref{eq-wide-p} is simply obtained by taking all the left endpoints of the intervals $I \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$, except $1$.
nodes.statement_short: The estimated change points are the left endpoints (other than 1) of the intervals of the optimal partition.

nodes.name: Dynamic programming solves the minimal partition problem
nodes.statement: The optimization problem \eqref{eq-wide-p} is known as the \emph{minimal partition problem} and can be solved using dynamic programming with an overall computational cost of order $O(n^2 \mathcal T(n))$, where $\mathcal T(n)$ denotes the computational cost of solving $\mathcal{L}(I)$ with $|I| = n$ \citep[see e.g.~Algorithm 1 in][]{FriedrichEtal2008}.
nodes.statement_short: The minimal partition problem is solvable by dynamic programming in $O(n^2\mathcal T(n))$ time.

nodes.name: Lasso-based segment loss
nodes.statement_short: Segment loss is the residual sum of squares of a Lasso fit on the segment with penalty scaled by $\sqrt{\max\{|I|,\log(n\vee p)\}}$.

nodes.name: Segment loss
nodes.statement: \mathcal L(I) = \sum_{t \in I}(y_t - x_t^{\top} \widehat \beta^\lambda_I)^2,
nodes.label: eq-loss-1

nodes.name: Interval Lasso estimator
nodes.statement:
\widehat \beta^\lambda_I = arg\,min_{v \in \mathbb R^p} \bigg\{\sum_{t \in I} (y_t - x_t^{\top}v)^2  \nonumber \\
		+ \lambda \sqrt{\max\{|I|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \| v\|_1\bigg\},
nodes.label: eq-beta-1

nodes.name: Local Refinement
nodes.statement_short: Refine each preliminary change point by a group-Lasso penalized two-segment fit on a shrunken window between its neighbouring estimates.

nodes.name: Initialize boundary estimates
nodes.statement: $(\widetilde{\eta}_0, \widetilde{\eta}_{\widetilde{K} + 1}) \leftarrow (0, n)$

nodes.name: Loop over preliminary change points
Shrunken working interval
nodes.statement: $(s_k, e_k) \leftarrow (2\widetilde{\eta}_{k-1}/3 + \widetilde{\eta}_{k}/3, \widetilde{\eta}_{k}/3 + 2\widetilde{\eta}_{k+1}/3)$
nodes.statement_short: Set the working interval $(s_k,e_k)$ to a shrunken window between neighbouring preliminary estimates.

nodes.name: Group-Lasso two-segment fit
nodes.statement_short: Re-estimate the change point by minimizing a two-segment least squares loss with a group Lasso penalty.

nodes.name: Shrinking constants are not special
nodes.statement: \Cref{algorithm:LR} takes a sequence of preliminary change point estimators $\{\widetilde{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\widetilde{K}}$, and refines each of the estimator $\widetilde{\eta}_k$ within the interval $(s_k, e_k)$, which is a shrunken version of $(\widetilde{\eta}_{k-1}, \widetilde{\eta}_{k+1})$ (the constants $2/3$ and $1/3$ specifying the shrinking factor in the definition of $(\widetilde{\eta}_{k-1}, \widetilde{\eta}_{k+1})$ are not special and can be replaced by other values without affecting the rates).
nodes.statement_short: Each estimate is refined in a shrunken window; the shrinking constants 2/3 and 1/3 can be changed without affecting rates.

nodes.name: High-dimensional coefficient assumptions
nodes.statement:
Consider the model defined in \Cref{assume:change point regression model}. We assume that, for some fixed positive constants $C_{\beta}$, $c_x$, $C_x$, $\xi$, and   $C_{\mathrm{SNR}} $ the following holds:

\noindent \textbf{a.} (Sparsity).  Let $d_0 = |S|$.  There exists a subset $S \subset \{1, \ldots, p\}$ such that 
			\[
				\beta_t^*(j) = 0, \quad t = 1, \ldots, n, \quad j \in S^c = \{1, \ldots, p\} \setminus S.
			\]
			  
			
\noindent \textbf{b.} (Boundedness). For some absolute constant $C_{\beta} > 0$, $\max_{t = 1, \ldots, n} \|\beta_t^*\|_{\infty} \leq C_{\beta}$.
	
\noindent \textbf{c.} (Minimal eigenvalue).  We have that $\Lambda_{\min}(\Sigma) = c_x^2 > 0$  and $\max_{j = 1, \ldots, p} (\Sigma)_{jj} = C_x^2 > 0$.

\noindent \textbf{d.} (Signal-to-noise ratio).  Let $\kappa= \min_{k = 1, \ldots, K + 1} \| \beta^*_{\eta_k} - \beta^*_{\eta_{k-1}}\|_2$ and $\Delta= \min_{k = 1, \ldots, K + 1} (\eta_{k} - \eta_{k-1})$ be the minimal jump size and minimal spacing defined as follows, respectively. Then,
			\begin{equation} \Delta \kappa^2 \geq C_{\mathrm{SNR}} d_0^2 K \sigma^2_{\varepsilon}\log^{1 + \xi}(n\vee p).
			\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Sparsity, bounded coefficients, minimal eigenvalue of $\Sigma$, and the signal-to-noise condition $\Delta\kappa^2 \gtrsim d_0^2 K \sigma_\varepsilon^2 \log^{1+\xi}(n\vee p)$.
nodes.label: assume:high dim coefficient

nodes.name: Signal-to-noise ratio condition
nodes.statement: \Delta \kappa^2 \geq C_{\mathrm{SNR}} d_0^2 K \sigma^2_{\varepsilon}\log^{1 + \xi}(n\vee p).
nodes.label: eq:snr

nodes.name: SNR condition matches univariate lower bound
nodes.statement: Interestingly, if $K = d_0 = 1$, \eqref{eq:snr} reduces to $\Delta \kappa^2 \sigma^{-2}_{\epsilon}\gtrsim \log^{1 + \xi}(n \vee p)$, matching the information theoretic lower bound  (up to constants and logarithmic terms) for the univariate mean change point detection problem \citep[see e.g.][]{chan2013, FrickEtal2014, wang2018univariate}.

nodes.name: Effective sample size bound
nodes.statement:
\Delta & \geq \frac{C_{\mathrm{SNR}} d_0^2 K \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log^{1 + \xi}(n \vee p)}{\kappa^2} \nonumber \\
		& \geq 	\frac{C_{\mathrm{SNR}} d_0^2 K \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log^{1 + \xi}(n \vee p)}{4C_{\beta}^2 d_0} \nonumber \\
		& \geq \frac{C_{\mathrm{SNR}}}{4C_{\beta}^2} d_0 K \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p),
nodes.label: eq-eff-size

nodes.name: Effective sample size interpretation
nodes.statement:
If $\Delta = \Theta (n)$ and $K=O(1)$, then \eqref{eq-eff-size}  becomes $ n \gtrsim d_0 \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p)$, 
   which  resembles the effective sample size condition needed in the Lasso estimation literature.

nodes.name: Normalized jump size form of the SNR condition
nodes.statement:
Another way to interpret the signal-to-noise ratio \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{d}) is to introduce a normalized jump size $\kappa_0 = \kappa/\sqrt{d_0}$, which leads to the equivalent condition
	\[
		\Delta \kappa_0^2 \geq C_{\mathrm{SNR}} d_0 K \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p).
	\]

nodes.name: Role of the constant xi
nodes.statement:
The constant $\xi$ is needed to guarantee consistency when $\Delta$ is of the same irder as $n$ but  can be set to zero if $\Delta = o(n)$.  We may instead replace it with a weaker condition of the form
	\[
		\Delta \kappa^2 \gtrsim C_{\mathrm{SNR}} d_0^2 K \{\log(n \vee p) + a_n\},
	\]
	where $a_n \to \infty$ arbitrarily slow as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Localization rate of the dynamic programming estimator
nodes.statement:
Assume \Cref{assume:change point regression model} and the conditions in  \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}. Then,
the change point estimators $\{\widetilde{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\widehat{K}}$ obtained as a solution to the dynamic programming optimization problem given in \eqref{eq-wide-p}, \eqref{eq-loss-1}, and \eqref{eq-beta-1}  with tuning parameters
	\[
		\lambda = C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{d_0 \log(n \vee p)}
	\]
	and
	\[
		\gamma = C_{\gamma}\sigma_{\epsilon}^2 (K+1) d^2_0 \log(n \vee p),
	\]
	are such that
	\begin{align} & \mathbb{P}\left\{\widehat K = K, \, \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K}|\widetilde{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq  \frac{KC_{\epsilon}d_0^2 \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log(n \vee p)}{\kappa^2} \right\} \nonumber\\ 
		& \hspace{1cm}\geq 1 - C(n \vee p)^{-c},
	\end{align}
	where $C_{\lambda}, C_{\gamma}, C_{\epsilon}, C, c > 0$ are absolute constants depending only on $C_{\beta}, C_x$, and $c_x$.
nodes.statement_short: With suitable $\lambda,\gamma$, the DP estimator recovers $K$ and localizes each change point within $K d_0^2\sigma_\varepsilon^2\log(n\vee p)/\kappa^2$ w.h.p.
assumptions: Assume \Cref{assume:change point regression model} and the conditions in  \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}.
\gamma = C_{\gamma}\sigma_{\epsilon}^2 (K+1) d^2_0 \log(n \vee p),
conclusions:
\mathbb{P}\left\{\widehat K = K, \, \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K}|\widetilde{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq  \frac{KC_{\epsilon}d_0^2 \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log(n \vee p)}{\kappa^2} \right\} \nonumber\\ 
		& \hspace{1cm}\geq 1 - C(n \vee p)^{-c},
nodes.label: eq:DP consistent for regression

nodes.name: DP localization bound
nodes.statement:
& \mathbb{P}\left\{\widehat K = K, \, \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K}|\widetilde{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq  \frac{KC_{\epsilon}d_0^2 \sigma^2_{\epsilon} \log(n \vee p)}{\kappa^2} \right\} \nonumber\\ 
		& \hspace{1cm}\geq 1 - C(n \vee p)^{-c},
nodes.label: eq-lm-thm-1

nodes.name: DP localization error is vanishing
nodes.statement_short: Under the SNR condition the localization error relative to $\Delta$ tends to zero, so the DP estimator is consistent.

nodes.name: Local refinement needs only a crude initializer
nodes.statement: Interestingly, the initial estimators need not be consistent in order for local refinement to work: all that is required is essentially that the each of the working intervals in \Cref{algorithm:LR} contains one and only one true change point. This fact allows us to refine the search within each working intervals separately, yielding better rates.

nodes.name: Working intervals contain exactly one change point
nodes.statement_short: With DP outputs as initializers, each working interval $(s_k,e_k)$ of local refinement lies strictly around the true change point $\eta_k$.
assumptions: if we use the outputs of \eqref{eq-wide-p}, \eqref{eq-loss-1}, and \eqref{eq-beta-1} as the inputs of \Cref{algorithm:LR}

nodes.name: Localization rate of local refinement
nodes.statement:
Assume the same conditions of \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression}.

Let $\{\widetilde{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{K}$ be a set of time points satisfying
	\begin{equation} \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K} |\widetilde{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq \Delta/7.
	\end{equation}
	Let $\{\widehat{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\widehat{K}}$ be the change point estimators generated from \Cref{algorithm:LR} with $\{\widetilde{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{K}$ and 
	\[
		\zeta = C_{\zeta}\sqrt{\log(n \vee p)}
	\]
	as inputs.  Then,
	\begin{align*}
		& \mathbb{P}\left\{\widehat K = K, \, \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K}|\hat{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq \frac{C_{\epsilon} d_0 \log(n \vee p)}{\kappa^2} \right\} \\
		& \hspace{1cm}\geq 1 - Cn^{-c},
	\end{align*}
	where $C_{\zeta}, C_{\epsilon}, C, c > 0$ are absolute constants depending only on $C_{\beta}, \mathcal{M}$ and $c_x$.
nodes.statement_short: Given initial estimates within $\Delta/7$ of the truth, local refinement localizes each change point within $d_0\log(n\vee p)/\kappa^2$ w.h.p.
assumptions: Assume the same conditions of \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression}.
Let $\{\widetilde{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{K}$ be a set of time points satisfying

Let $\{\widehat{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\widehat{K}}$ be the change point estimators generated from \Cref{algorithm:LR} with $\{\widetilde{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{K}$ and 
	\[
		\zeta = C_{\zeta}\sqrt{\log(n \vee p)}
	\]
	as inputs.
conclusions:
\mathbb{P}\left\{\widehat K = K, \, \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K}|\hat{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq \frac{C_{\epsilon} d_0 \log(n \vee p)}{\kappa^2} \right\} \\
		& \hspace{1cm}\geq 1 - Cn^{-c},
nodes.label: cor-lr-3

nodes.name: Initial estimator accuracy condition
nodes.statement: \max_{k = 1, \ldots, K} |\widetilde{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \leq \Delta/7.
nodes.label: eq-lr-cond-1

nodes.name: Why local refinement removes the dependence on K
nodes.statement:
Compared to the localization error given in \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression}, the improved localization error guaranteed by the local refinement algorithm does not have a direct dependence on $K$, the number of change points. The intuition for this is as follows.
First, due to the nature of the change point detection problem, there is a natural group structure.  This justifies the use of the group Lasso-type penalty, which reduces the localization error by bringing down $d_0^2$ to $d_0$. Second, using condition \eqref{eq-lr-cond-1}, there is one and only one true change point in every working interval used by the local refinement algorithm. The true change points can then be estimated separately using $K$ independent searches, in such a way that the final localization rate that does not depend on the number of searches, namely $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Group structure lets group Lasso reduce $d_0^2$ to $d_0$, and one change point per working interval removes the factor $K$.

nodes.name: Comparison with wild binary segmentation accuracy
nodes.statement: With these additional tuning parameters, Theorem~1 in \cite{wang2019statistically} achieved the same statistical accuracy in terms of the localization error rate as   \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression} above.

nodes.name: Computational cost comparison with WBS
nodes.statement: In terms of computational cost, the methods in \cite{wang2019statistically} are of order $O(K^2 n\cdot \text{Lasso}(n))$, where $K$, $n$ and $\text{Lasso}(n)$ denote the number of change points, the sample size and the computational cost of Lasso algorithm with sample size $n$, respectively, while the dynamic programming approach of this paper   is of order $O(n^2 \cdot \text{Lasso}(n))$.  Thus, when $K \lesssim \sqrt{n}$, the algorithm in \cite{wang2019statistically} is computationally more efficient, but when $K \gtrsim \sqrt{n}$, the method in this paper has smaller complexity.
nodes.statement_short: WBS-based methods cost $O(K^2 n\,\text{Lasso}(n))$ versus $O(n^2\,\text{Lasso}(n))$ for DP, so DP is cheaper when $K \gtrsim \sqrt n$.

nodes.name: Leonardi-Buhlmann localization bound
nodes.statement: \sum_{k = 1}^K |\hat{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \lesssim \frac{d_0^2 \sqrt{n \log(np)}}{\kappa^2}.
nodes.label: eq-bul

nodes.name: Sum of localization errors of DP
nodes.statement:
Using a worst-case upper bound, \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression} yields that 
	 	\[
	 		\sum_{k = 1}^K |\hat{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \lesssim \frac{K^2 d_0^2 \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \log(n\vee p)}{\kappa^2}.
	 	\]

nodes.name: Sum of localization errors after local refinement
nodes.statement:
In light of \Cref{cor-lr-3}, this error bound can be sharpened, using the local refinement \Cref{algorithm:LR} to
	 	\[
	 		\sum_{k = 1}^K |\hat{\eta}_k - \eta_k| \lesssim \frac{K d_0 \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \log(n\vee p)}{\kappa^2}.
	 	\]

nodes.name: Rates better than Leonardi-Buhlmann
nodes.statement: As long as $K^2 \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{n}{\log(np)}}$, or, using the local refinement algorithm,  $K\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{n}{\log(np)}}$, our localization rates are better than the one implied by \eqref{eq-bul}.

nodes.name: Comparison of assumptions with Leonardi-Buhlmann
nodes.statement:
For instance, the conditions in Theorem~3.1 of \cite{leonardi2016computationally} imply, in our notation, that condition 
	 		\[
	 			\Delta \gtrsim \sqrt{n \log(p)}
	 		\]
	 		is needed for consistency,
	 		even if the sparsity parameter $d_0 = \Theta(1)$.  However in our case, in view of \eqref{eq:snr}, if we assume $d_0 = \kappa = \Theta(1)$, then we only require $\Delta \gtrsim \log^{1 + \xi}(n\vee p)$ for consistency.

nodes.name: Detection lower bound
nodes.statement:
Let $\{(x_t, y_t)\}_{t = 1}^T \subset \mathbb{R}^p \times \mathbb{R}$ satisfy \Cref{assume:change point regression model} and \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}, with $K = 1$.  In addition, assume that $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^n \stackrel{\mbox{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, I_p)$ and $\{ \varepsilon_t \}_{t=1}^n \stackrel{\mbox{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2)$.  Let $P^T_{\kappa, \Delta, \sigma_{\varepsilon}, d}$ be the corresponding joint distribution.  For any $0 < c < \frac{2}{8e+1}$, consider the class of distributions
	\begin{align*}
		\mathcal{P} = \Big\{P^T_{\kappa, \Delta, \sigma_{\varepsilon}, d}: \, \Delta = \min\left\{\lfloor cd_0 \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2\kappa^{-2}\rfloor, \, \lfloor T/4\rfloor \right\},\\
		 2cd_0\max\{d_0, 2\} \leq \Delta\Big\}.
	\end{align*}
	There exists a $T(c)$, which depends on $c$, such that for all $T \geq T(c)$,
	\[
		\inf_{\widehat{\eta}} \sup_{P \in \mathcal{P}} \mathbb{E}_P(|\widehat{\eta} - \eta(P)|) \geq \Delta,
	\]
	where $\eta(P)$ is the location of the change point of distribution $P$ and the infimum is over all estimators of the change point.
nodes.statement_short: If $\kappa^2\Delta \lesssim d_0\sigma_\varepsilon^2$, the minimax localization error is at least $\Delta$: no estimator is consistent.

For any $0 < c < \frac{2}{8e+1}$, consider the class of distributions
	\begin{align*}
		\mathcal{P} = \Big\{P^T_{\kappa, \Delta, \sigma_{\varepsilon}, d}: \, \Delta = \min\left\{\lfloor cd_0 \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2\kappa^{-2}\rfloor, \, \lfloor T/4\rfloor \right\},\\
		 2cd_0\max\{d_0, 2\} \leq \Delta\Big\}.
for all $T \geq T(c)$
nodes.label: lem-reg-lb-1

nodes.name: Localization error is not vanishing in the low SNR regime
nodes.statement:
\Cref{lem-reg-lb-1} shows that if $\kappa^2 \Delta \lesssim d_0 \sigma^2_{\varepsilon}$, then 
	\[
		\frac{\inf_{\widehat{\eta}} \sup_{P \in \mathcal{P}} \mathbb{E}_P(|\widehat{\eta} - \eta(P)|)}{\Delta} \geq 1,
	\]
	which implies that the localization error is not a vanishing fraction of $\Delta$ as the sample size grows unbounded.

nodes.name: Localization lower bound
nodes.statement:
Let $\{(x_t, y_t)\}_{t = 1}^T \subset \mathbb{R}^p \times \mathbb{R}$ satisfy \Cref{assume:change point regression model} and \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}, with $K = 1$.  In addition, assume $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^n \stackrel{\mbox{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, I_p)$ and $\{ \varepsilon_t \}_{t=1}^n \stackrel{\mbox{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\varepsilon})$.  Let $P^T_{\kappa, \Delta, \sigma_{\varepsilon}, d}$ be the corresponding joint distribution.  For any diverging sequence $\zeta_T$, consider the class of distributions
	\[
		\mathcal{P} = \left\{P^T_{\kappa, \Delta, \sigma_{\varepsilon}, d}: \, \Delta = \min\left\{\lfloor \zeta_T d_0 \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2\kappa^{-2}\rfloor, \, \lfloor T/4\rfloor \right\} \right\}.
	\]
	Then 
	\[
		\inf_{\widehat{\eta}} \sup_{P \in \mathcal{P}} \mathbb{E}_P(|\widehat{\eta} - \eta(P)|)\geq \frac{cd_0 \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2}{\kappa^2},
	\]
	where $\eta(P)$ is the location of the change point of distribution $P$, the infimum is over all estimators of the change point and $c > 0$ is an absolute constant.
nodes.statement_short: The minimax localization error is at least of order $d_0\sigma_\varepsilon^2/\kappa^2$.
assumptions: Let $\{(x_t, y_t)\}_{t = 1}^T \subset \mathbb{R}^p \times \mathbb{R}$ satisfy \Cref{assume:change point regression model} and \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}, with $K = 1$.
assume $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^n \stackrel{\mbox{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, I_p)$ and $\{ \varepsilon_t \}_{t=1}^n \stackrel{\mbox{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\varepsilon})$

For any diverging sequence $\zeta_T$, consider the class of distributions
	\[
		\mathcal{P} = \left\{P^T_{\kappa, \Delta, \sigma_{\varepsilon}, d}: \, \Delta = \min\left\{\lfloor \zeta_T d_0 \sigma_{\varepsilon}^2\kappa^{-2}\rfloor, \, \lfloor T/4\rfloor \right\} \right\}.
nodes.label: lem-reg-lb-2

nodes.name: Phase diagram of change point localization
nodes.statement: Recalling all the results we have obtained, the change point localization task is either impossible when $\kappa^2 \Delta \lesssim d_0 \sigma^2_{\varepsilon}$ (in the sense that  no algorithm is guaranteed to be consistent) or, when $\kappa^2 \Delta \gtrsim d_0^2 K \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p)$, it can be solved by our algorithms at nearly a minimax optimal rate.

nodes.name: Intermediate signal-to-noise regime
nodes.statement:
In the intermediate case 
\[
d_0 \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \lesssim \kappa^2 \Delta \lesssim d^2_0 K \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p) 
\]
we are unable to provide a result one way or another.
nodes.statement_short: Whether change points can be consistently localized when $d_0\sigma^2 \lesssim \kappa^2\Delta \lesssim d_0^2K\sigma^2\log^{1+\xi}(n\vee p)$ is left open.

nodes.name: Weaker SNR condition for bounded jump size
nodes.statement:
However, we remark that, if in addition, in \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression}, we assume $\kappa \leq C$, for an absolute constant $C > 0$, then we are able to weaken the condition from $\kappa^2 \Delta \gtrsim d_0^2 K \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p)$ to $\kappa^2 \Delta \gtrsim d_0 K \sigma^2_{\varepsilon} \log^{1+\xi}(n \vee p)$, by almost identical arguments.  This shows that, under the additional conditions 
	\[
		\max\{\kappa, \, K\} \leq C,
	\]
	for an absolute constant $C > 0$, the condition is nearly optimal, off by a logarithmic factor.
nodes.statement_short: If $\kappa$ is bounded the SNR condition can be weakened by a factor $d_0$; with bounded $K$ too it is optimal up to logs.

nodes.name: Scaled Hausdorff distance
nodes.statement:
The evaluation metric considered is the scaled Hausdorff distance between the estimators $\{\hat{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\hat K}$ and the truth $\{\eta_k\}_{k =1}^K$.  To be specific, we report
$\mathit{d}(\hat{\mathcal{C}},\mathcal{C}) = n^{-1}\mathcal{D}(\hat{\mathcal{C}},\mathcal{C})$, where 
    \[
        \mathcal{D}(\hat{\mathcal{C}},\mathcal{C}) = \max\{\max_{\hat{\eta} \in \hat{\mathcal{C}}}\min_{\eta \in \mathcal{C}}|\hat{\eta} - \eta|,\max_{\eta \in \mathcal{C}}\min_{\hat{\eta} \in \hat{\mathcal{C}}}|\hat{\eta} - \eta|\},
    \]
     $\mathcal{C} = \{\eta_k\}_{k =1}^K$ and $\hat{\mathcal{C}} = \{\hat{\eta}_k\}_{k = 1}^{\hat K}$.
nodes.statement_short: Error metric: Hausdorff distance between estimated and true change point sets, divided by $n$.

nodes.name: Cross-validation tuning parameter selection
nodes.statement: We adopt a cross-validation approach to choosing tuning parameters.  Let samples with odd indices be the training set and even ones be the validation set.  Recall that for the DP, we have two tuning parameters $\lambda$ and $\gamma$, which we tune using a brute-force grid search.  For each pair of tuning parameters, we conduct DP on the training set and obtain estimated change points.  Within each estimated segment of the training set, we obtain $\hat{\beta_t}$ by \eqref{eq-beta-1}.  On the validation set, let $\hat{y_t} = x_t^{\top} \hat{\beta}_t$ and calculate the validation loss $(n/2)^{-1} \sum_{t \mod 2 \equiv 0}(\hat{y}_t - y_t)^2$.  The pair $(\lambda, \gamma)$ is chosen to be the one corresponding to the lowest validation loss.
nodes.statement_short: Grid search over $(\lambda,\gamma)$: fit DP on odd-indexed samples and choose the pair minimizing prediction loss on even-indexed samples.
output: The pair $(\lambda, \gamma)$ is chosen to be the one corresponding to the lowest validation loss.

nodes.name: Train/validation split
nodes.statement: Let samples with odd indices be the training set and even ones be the validation set.
nodes.statement_short: Split samples into odd-indexed training and even-indexed validation sets.

nodes.name: Grid over tuning parameters
nodes.statement: Recall that for the DP, we have two tuning parameters $\lambda$ and $\gamma$, which we tune using a brute-force grid search.
nodes.statement_short: Search a grid of $(\lambda,\gamma)$ pairs.

nodes.name: Run DP on training set
nodes.statement: For each pair of tuning parameters, we conduct DP on the training set and obtain estimated change points.
nodes.statement_short: Run the DP estimator on the training set.

nodes.name: Estimate segment coefficients
nodes.statement: Within each estimated segment of the training set, we obtain $\hat{\beta_t}$ by \eqref{eq-beta-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Fit the interval Lasso on each estimated segment.

nodes.name: Validation loss
nodes.statement: On the validation set, let $\hat{y_t} = x_t^{\top} \hat{\beta}_t$ and calculate the validation loss $(n/2)^{-1} \sum_{t \mod 2 \equiv 0}(\hat{y}_t - y_t)^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute mean squared prediction error on the validation set.

nodes.name: Choose best pair
nodes.statement: The pair $(\lambda, \gamma)$ is chosen to be the one corresponding to the lowest validation loss.
nodes.statement_short: Pick the pair with smallest validation loss.

nodes.name: Structure of the DP partition
nodes.statement:
Under the same conditions in \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression} and letting $\widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ being the solution to \eqref{eq-wide-p}, the following hold with probability at least $1 - C(n \vee p)^{-c}$. 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item [(i)] For each interval  $\widehat I = (s, e] \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$    containing one and only one true change point $\eta$, it must be the case that
			\[
				\min\{e - \eta, \eta - s\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{d_0 \lambda^2 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right),
			\]
			where $C_{\epsilon} > 0$ is an absolute constant;
		\item [(ii)] for each interval  $\widehat I = (s, e] \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ containing exactly two true change points, say  $\eta_1 < \eta_2$, it must be the case that
			\[
				\max\{e - \eta_2, \eta_1 - s\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{d_0 \lambda^2 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right), 	
			\]  
			where $C_{\epsilon} > 0$ is an absolute constant;
		\item [(iii)] for all consecutive intervals $\widehat I$ and $\widehat {J}$ in $\widehat{P}$, the interval $\widehat I \cup \widehat{J}$ contains at least one true change point; and
		\item [(iv)] no interval $\widehat I \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ contains strictly more than two true change points.
	 \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: W.h.p. every interval of the DP partition contains at most two change points, with boundary distances to them bounded by $(d_0\lambda^2+\gamma)/\kappa^2$, and no two consecutive intervals are change-free.
assumptions: Under the same conditions in \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression} and letting $\widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ being the solution to \eqref{eq-wide-p}
conclusions:
For each interval  $\widehat I = (s, e] \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$    containing one and only one true change point $\eta$, it must be the case that
			\[
				\min\{e - \eta, \eta - s\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{d_0 \lambda^2 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right),
			\]
			where $C_{\epsilon} > 0$ is an absolute constant;

for each interval  $\widehat I = (s, e] \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ containing exactly two true change points, say  $\eta_1 < \eta_2$, it must be the case that
			\[
				\max\{e - \eta_2, \eta_1 - s\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{d_0 \lambda^2 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right), 	
			\]  
			where $C_{\epsilon} > 0$ is an absolute constant;
for all consecutive intervals $\widehat I$ and $\widehat {J}$ in $\widehat{P}$, the interval $\widehat I \cup \widehat{J}$ contains at least one true change point;
no interval $\widehat I \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ contains strictly more than two true change points.
nodes.label: proposition:dp step 1

nodes.name: DP recovers the number of change points
nodes.statement: Under the same conditions in \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression}, with $\widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ being the solution to \eqref{eq-wide-p}, satisfying $K \leq |\widehat{\mathcal{P}}| \leq 3K$, then with probability at least $1 - C(n \vee p)^{-c}$, it holds that $|\widehat{\mathcal{P}}| = K$.
nodes.statement_short: If the DP partition has between $K$ and $3K$ intervals, then w.h.p. it has exactly $K$.
assumptions: Under the same conditions in \Cref{eq:DP consistent for regression}, with $\widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ being the solution to \eqref{eq-wide-p}, satisfying $K \leq |\widehat{\mathcal{P}}| \leq 3K$
conclusions: with probability at least $1 - C(n \vee p)^{-c}$, it holds that $|\widehat{\mathcal{P}}| = K$.
nodes.label: prop-2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: It follows from \Cref{proposition:dp step 1} that, $K \leq |\widehat{\mathcal{P}}| \leq 3K$.  This combined with \Cref{prop-2} completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Proposition 5 (which gives $K \le |\widehat{\mathcal P}| \le 3K$) with Proposition 6.

nodes.name: Sketch of the proofs of Propositions 5 and 6
nodes.statement:
The key ingredients of the proofs of both Propositions~\ref{proposition:dp step 1} and \ref{prop-2} are two types of deviation inequalities.  
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \textbf{Restricted eigenvalues.}  In the literature on sparse regression, there are several versions of the restricted eigenvalue conditions \citep[see, e.g.][]{buhlmann2011statistics}.  In our analysis, such conditions amount to controlling the probability of the event
			\[
				\mathcal{E}_I = \left\{\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I} \bigl(x_t^{\top}v\bigr)^2} \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v\|_1, \quad \forall v \in \mathbb{R}^p \right\},
			\]
			which is done in \Cref{lem-RE}.
		\item \textbf{Deviations bounds of scaled noise.}  In addition, we need to control the deviations of the quantities of the form
			\begin{equation} \left\|\sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t \right\|_{\infty}.
			\end{equation}
			See \Cref{lem-x-bound}.
	\end{itemize}
	
In standard analyses of the performance of the Lasso estimator, as detailed e.g.~in Section 6.2 of \cite{buhlmann2011statistics}, the combination of restricted eigenvalues conditions and large probability bounds on the noise lead to oracle inequalities for the estimation and prediction errors in situations in which there exists no change point and the data are independent. We have extended this line of arguments to the present, more challenging settings, to derive analogous oracle inequalities.  We emphasize a few points in this regard.

	\begin{itemize}
		\item In standard analyses of the Lasso estimator, where there is one and only one true coefficient vector, the magnitude of $\lambda$ is determined as a high-probability upper bound to \eqref{eq-lambda-rate-determ}.  However in our situation, in order to control the $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-loss of the estimators $\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I$, where the interval $I$ contains more than one true coefficient vectors, the value of $\lambda$ needs to be inflated by a factor of $\sqrt{d_0}$.  This is detailed in \Cref{lemma:oracle 2}; see, in particular, \eqref{eq-lem10-pf-1}.
		\item The magnitude of the tuning parameter $\gamma$ is determined based on an appropriate oracle inequality for the Lasso and on the number of true change points; more precisely, $\gamma$ can be derived as a high-probability bound for 
			\[
				\left|\sum_{t \in I} \bigl\{(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I)^2 - (y_t - x_t^{\top}\beta_t^*)^2\bigr\}\right|.
			\]
			See \Cref{lemma:RSS lasso} for details.
			
			The fact that $\gamma$ is linear in the number of change point $K$ is to prompt the consistency.  This is shown in \eqref{eq:Khat=K} in the proof of \Cref{prop-2}. 
		\item The final localization error is obtained by the following calculations.  Assume that there exists one and only one true change point $\eta \in I = (s, e]$.  Define $I_1 = (s, \eta]$ and $I_2 = (\eta_1, e]$.  Let $\beta^*_{I_1}$ and $\beta^*_{I_2}$ be the two true coefficient vectors in $I_1$ and $I_2$, respectively.   For readability, below we will omit all constants here and use the symbol $\lessapprox$ to denote an inequality up to hidden universal constants.  We first assume by contradiction that
			\begin{equation} \min\{|I_1|, |I_2|\} \gtrsim d_0 \log(n \vee p),
 			\end{equation}
 			then use oracle inequalities to establish that
			\begin{align}
				& \sum_{t \in I_1} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})\}^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})\}^2 \nonumber \\
				\lessapprox & \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I_1|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} + \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I_2|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} + \gamma \nonumber\\				
				\lessapprox & \lambda\sqrt{|I_1|} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} + \lambda\sqrt{|I_2|} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} + \gamma \nonumber\\
				\lessapprox & \frac{\lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + |I_1| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|_2^2 + |I_2| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2}\|_2^2 + \lambda^2 + (|I_1|^2 + |I_2|^2)\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1^2  + \gamma, \end{align}
			where the second inequality follows \eqref{eq-main-i-cond} and the third inequality follows from $2ab \leq a^2 + b^2$ and from setting
			\[
				a = \lambda\sqrt{d_0} \quad \mbox{and} \quad b = \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|_2.
			\]
			Next we apply the restricted eigenvalue conditions along with standard arguments from the Lasso literature to establish that 
			\begin{align}
				& \sum_{t \in I_1} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})\}^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})\}^2 \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} \geq c_x^2 |I_1| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|^2 + c_x^2 |I_2| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2}\|^2 \geq c_x^2 \kappa^2 \epsilon, \end{align}
			where $\epsilon$ is an upper bound on the localization error.  Combining \eqref{eq-illustrate-upper} and \eqref{eq-illustrate-lower} leads to 
			\[
				\epsilon \lesssim \frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}.
			\]
		\item Finally, the signal-to-noise ratio condition that one needs to assume in order to obtain consistent localization rates is determined by setting $\epsilon \lesssim \Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Proof sketch: restricted eigenvalue and noise deviation bounds give Lasso oracle inequalities; contradiction on interval lengths yields $\epsilon \lesssim (\lambda^2 d_0+\gamma)/\kappa^2$.

nodes.name: Inflated lambda
nodes.statement: In standard analyses of the Lasso estimator, where there is one and only one true coefficient vector, the magnitude of $\lambda$ is determined as a high-probability upper bound to \eqref{eq-lambda-rate-determ}.  However in our situation, in order to control the $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-loss of the estimators $\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I$, where the interval $I$ contains more than one true coefficient vectors, the value of $\lambda$ needs to be inflated by a factor of $\sqrt{d_0}$.  This is detailed in \Cref{lemma:oracle 2}; see, in particular, \eqref{eq-lem10-pf-1}.

nodes.name: Choice of gamma
nodes.statement:
The magnitude of the tuning parameter $\gamma$ is determined based on an appropriate oracle inequality for the Lasso and on the number of true change points; more precisely, $\gamma$ can be derived as a high-probability bound for 
			\[

nodes.name: Localization error calculation
nodes.statement:
The final localization error is obtained by the following calculations.  Assume that there exists one and only one true change point $\eta \in I = (s, e]$.  Define $I_1 = (s, \eta]$ and $I_2 = (\eta_1, e]$.  Let $\beta^*_{I_1}$ and $\beta^*_{I_2}$ be the two true coefficient vectors in $I_1$ and $I_2$, respectively.   For readability, below we will omit all constants here and use the symbol $\lessapprox$ to denote an inequality up to hidden universal constants.  We first assume by contradiction that
			\begin{equation} \min\{|I_1|, |I_2|\} \gtrsim d_0 \log(n \vee p),
 			\end{equation}
 			then use oracle inequalities to establish that
			\begin{align}
				& \sum_{t \in I_1} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})\}^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})\}^2 \nonumber \\
				\lessapprox & \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I_1|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} + \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I_2|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} + \gamma \nonumber\\				
				\lessapprox & \lambda\sqrt{|I_1|} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} + \lambda\sqrt{|I_2|} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} + \gamma \nonumber\\
				\lessapprox & \frac{\lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + |I_1| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|_2^2 + |I_2| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2}\|_2^2 + \lambda^2 + (|I_1|^2 + |I_2|^2)\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1^2  + \gamma, \end{align}
			where the second inequality follows \eqref{eq-main-i-cond} and the third inequality follows from $2ab \leq a^2 + b^2$ and from setting
			\[
				a = \lambda\sqrt{d_0} \quad \mbox{and} \quad b = \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|_2.
			\]
			Next we apply the restricted eigenvalue conditions along with standard arguments from the Lasso literature to establish that 
			\begin{align}
				& \sum_{t \in I_1} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})\}^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})\}^2 \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} \geq c_x^2 |I_1| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|^2 + c_x^2 |I_2| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2}\|^2 \geq c_x^2 \kappa^2 \epsilon, \end{align}
			where $\epsilon$ is an upper bound on the localization error.  Combining \eqref{eq-illustrate-upper} and \eqref{eq-illustrate-lower} leads to 
			\[
				\epsilon \lesssim \frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}.
			\]
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction plus oracle upper and restricted-eigenvalue lower bounds give $\epsilon \lesssim (\lambda^2 d_0+\gamma)/\kappa^2$.

nodes.name: SNR condition
nodes.statement: Finally, the signal-to-noise ratio condition that one needs to assume in order to obtain consistent localization rates is determined by setting $\epsilon \lesssim \Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: The SNR condition comes from requiring $\epsilon \lesssim \Delta$.

nodes.name: Set up single change point interval
nodes.statement: The final localization error is obtained by the following calculations.  Assume that there exists one and only one true change point $\eta \in I = (s, e]$.  Define $I_1 = (s, \eta]$ and $I_2 = (\eta_1, e]$.  Let $\beta^*_{I_1}$ and $\beta^*_{I_2}$ be the two true coefficient vectors in $I_1$ and $I_2$, respectively.   For readability, below we will omit all constants here and use the symbol $\lessapprox$ to denote an inequality up to hidden universal constants.
nodes.statement_short: Split $I$ at its unique change point into $I_1, I_2$.

nodes.name: Contradiction and oracle upper bound
nodes.statement:
We first assume by contradiction that
			\begin{equation} \min\{|I_1|, |I_2|\} \gtrsim d_0 \log(n \vee p),
 			\end{equation}
 			then use oracle inequalities to establish that
			\begin{align}
				& \sum_{t \in I_1} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})\}^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2} \{x_t^{\top} (\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})\}^2 \nonumber \\
				\lessapprox & \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I_1|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} + \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I_2|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} + \gamma \nonumber\\				
				\lessapprox & \lambda\sqrt{|I_1|} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} \nonumber \\
				& \hspace{2cm} + \lambda\sqrt{|I_2|} \big\{\sqrt{d_0}\|(\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2})(S)\|_2 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1\big\} + \gamma \nonumber\\
				\lessapprox & \frac{\lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + |I_1| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|_2^2 + |I_2| \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_2}\|_2^2 + \lambda^2 + (|I_1|^2 + |I_2|^2)\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1^2  + \gamma, \end{align}
			where the second inequality follows \eqref{eq-main-i-cond} and the third inequality follows from $2ab \leq a^2 + b^2$ and from setting
			\[
				a = \lambda\sqrt{d_0} \quad \mbox{and} \quad b = \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_{I_1}\|_2.
			\]
nodes.statement_short: Assume both pieces are long and bound the prediction error from above.

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalue lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound the prediction error by $c_x^2\kappa^2\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Combine bounds
nodes.statement:
Combining \eqref{eq-illustrate-upper} and \eqref{eq-illustrate-lower} leads to 
			\[
				\epsilon \lesssim \frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}.
			\]
nodes.statement_short: Combining yields $\epsilon \lesssim (\lambda^2 d_0+\gamma)/\kappa^2$.

nodes.name: Sketch of the proof of Corollary 2
nodes.statement:
The proofs related with \Cref{algorithm:LR} and \Cref{cor-lr-3} are all based on an oracle inequality of the group Lasso estimator.  Once it is established that
	\begin{equation} \sum_{t = s + 1}^e \|\widehat{\beta}_t - \beta^*_t\|_2^2 \leq \delta \leq \kappa \sqrt{\Delta},
	\end{equation}
	where $\delta \asymp d_0 \log(n \vee p)$ and where there is one and only one change point in the interval $(s, e]$ for both the sequence $\{\widehat{\beta}_t\}$ and $\{\beta^*_t\}$, then the final claim follows immediately that the refined localization error $\epsilon$ satisfies
	\[
		\epsilon \leq \delta/\kappa^2.
	\]
	The group Lasso penalty is deployed to prompt \eqref{eq-intuit-g-lasso} and the designs of the algorithm guarantee the desirability of each working interval.
nodes.statement_short: Proof sketch: a group Lasso oracle inequality on a working interval with one change point gives $\epsilon \le \delta/\kappa^2$.

nodes.statement: \sum_{t = s + 1}^e \|\widehat{\beta}_t - \beta^*_t\|_2^2 \leq \delta \leq \kappa \sqrt{\Delta},

Once it is established that
	\begin{equation} \sum_{t = s + 1}^e \|\widehat{\beta}_t - \beta^*_t\|_2^2 \leq \delta \leq \kappa \sqrt{\Delta},
	\end{equation}
	where $\delta \asymp d_0 \log(n \vee p)$ and where there is one and only one change point in the interval $(s, e]$ for both the sequence $\{\widehat{\beta}_t\}$ and $\{\beta^*_t\}$, then the final claim follows immediately that the refined localization error $\epsilon$ satisfies

nodes.name: Role of penalty and design
nodes.statement: The group Lasso penalty is deployed to prompt \eqref{eq-intuit-g-lasso} and the designs of the algorithm guarantee the desirability of each working interval.
nodes.statement_short: The group Lasso penalty and the working-interval design guarantee the conditions.

nodes.name: Interval-averaged coefficient
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, with some abuse of notation, for any interval $I \subset (0, n]$, we denote with $\beta^*_I = |I|^{-1}\sum_{t \in I} \beta^*_t$.

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalue event
nodes.statement:
For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{c}), for any interval $I \subset (0, n]$, it holds that
	\[
		\mathbb{P}\{\mathcal{E}_I\} \geq 1 - c_1 \exp(-c_2 |I|),
	\]
	where $c_1, c_2 > 0$ are absolute constants only depending on the distributions of covariants $\{x_t\}$, and
	\[
		\mathcal{E}_I = \left\{\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I} \bigl(x_t^{\top}v\bigr)^2} \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{ |I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v\|_1, \quad v \in \mathbb{R}^p \right\}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: With probability $1-c_1e^{-c_2|I|}$ the restricted-eigenvalue-type event $\mathcal{E}_I$ holds for any interval $I$.
assumptions: For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{c}), for any interval $I \subset (0, n]$
nodes.label: lem-RE

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7 (by reference)
nodes.statement: This follows from the same proof as Theorem~1 in \cite{raskutti2010restricted}, therefore we omit the proof of \Cref{lem-RE}.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as Theorem 1 of Raskutti et al. (2010); omitted.

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalue condition from Lemma 7
nodes.statement: For interval $I$ satisfying $|I| > C d_0\log(p)$, an immediate consequence of \Cref{lem-RE} is a restricted eigenvalue condition \citep[e.g.][]{van2009conditions, bickel2009simultaneous}.

nodes.name: Noise deviation event
nodes.statement:
For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{c}), for any interval $I \subset (0, n]$, it holds that for any 
	\[
		\lambda \geq \lambda_1 := C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{\log(n \vee p)},
	\]
	where $C_{\lambda} > 0$ is a large enough absolute constant such that, we have
	\[
		\mathbb{P}\{\mathcal{B}_I(\lambda)\} > 1 - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3},
	\]	
	where
	\[
		\mathcal{B}_I(\lambda) = \left\{\left\|\sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t \right\|_{\infty} \leq \lambda \sqrt{\max\{|I|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}}/8 \right\},
	\]
	where $c_3 > 0$ is an absolute constant depending only on the distributions of covariants $\{x_t\}$ and $\{\varepsilon_t\}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $\lambda \gtrsim \sigma_\varepsilon\sqrt{\log(n\vee p)}$, $\|\sum_{t\in I}\varepsilon_t x_t\|_\infty \le \lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I|,\log(n\vee p)\}}/8$ w.h.p.
assumptions: For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{c}), for any interval $I \subset (0, n]$
\lambda \geq \lambda_1 := C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{\log(n \vee p)},
nodes.label: lem-x-bound

nodes.name: Shorthand for the noise event
nodes.statement: For notational simplicity, we drop the dependence on $\lambda$ in the notation $\mathcal{B}_I(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8
nodes.statement:
Since $\varepsilon_t$'s are sub-Gaussian random variables and $x_t$'s are sub-Gaussian random vectors, we have that $\varepsilon_t x_t$'s are sub-Exponential random vectors with parameter $C_x \sigma_{\varepsilon}$ \citep[see e.g.~Lemma~2.7.7 in][]{vershynin2018high}.  It then follows from Bernstein's inequality \citep[see e.g.~Theorem~2.8.1 in][]{vershynin2018high} that for any $t > 0$,
		\[
			\mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|\sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t \right\|_{\infty} > t\right\} \leq 2p \exp\left\{-c \min\left\{\frac{t^2}{|I|C_x^2\sigma^2_{\varepsilon}}, \, \frac{t}{C_x \sigma_{\varepsilon}}\right\}\right\}.
		\]
		Taking 
		\[
			t = C_{\lambda}C_x/4 \sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{\log(n \vee p)} \sqrt{\max\{|I|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}}
		\] 
		yields that 
		\[
			\mathbb{P}\{\mathcal{B}_I\} > 1 - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3},
		\]
		where $c_3 > 0$ is an absolute constant depending on $C_{\lambda}, C_x, \sigma_{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Products $\varepsilon_t x_t$ are sub-exponential; Bernstein's inequality with a suitable threshold gives the bound.

nodes.name: Sub-exponential products
nodes.statement: Since $\varepsilon_t$'s are sub-Gaussian random variables and $x_t$'s are sub-Gaussian random vectors, we have that $\varepsilon_t x_t$'s are sub-Exponential random vectors with parameter $C_x \sigma_{\varepsilon}$ \citep[see e.g.~Lemma~2.7.7 in][]{vershynin2018high}.
nodes.statement_short: $\varepsilon_t x_t$ are sub-exponential.

nodes.name: Bernstein's inequality
nodes.statement:
It then follows from Bernstein's inequality \citep[see e.g.~Theorem~2.8.1 in][]{vershynin2018high} that for any $t > 0$,
		\[
			\mathbb{P}\left\{\left\|\sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t \right\|_{\infty} > t\right\} \leq 2p \exp\left\{-c \min\left\{\frac{t^2}{|I|C_x^2\sigma^2_{\varepsilon}}, \, \frac{t}{C_x \sigma_{\varepsilon}}\right\}\right\}.
		\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Bernstein's inequality to the sum.

nodes.name: Choose threshold
nodes.statement:
Taking 
		\[
			t = C_{\lambda}C_x/4 \sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{\log(n \vee p)} \sqrt{\max\{|I|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}}
		\] 
		yields that 
		\[
			\mathbb{P}\{\mathcal{B}_I\} > 1 - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3},
		\]
		where $c_3 > 0$ is an absolute constant depending on $C_{\lambda}, C_x, \sigma_{\varepsilon}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $t$ to obtain the stated probability.

nodes.name: Lasso estimation error on a stationary interval
nodes.statement:
For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{a}) and (\textbf{c}), if there exists no true change point in $I = (s, e]$, with $|I| > 288^2 C^2_x d_0 \log(n \vee p)/c_x^2$ and
	\[
		\lambda \geq \lambda_1 := C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{\log(n \vee p)},
	\] 
	where $C_{\lambda} >  0$ being an absolute constant, it holds that
	\begin{align*}
		& \mathbb{P}\left\{\bigl\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_I\bigr\|_2 \leq \frac{C_3 \lambda \sqrt{d_0}} {\sqrt{|I|}}, \quad \bigl\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_I\bigr\|_1 \leq \frac{C_3 \lambda d_0}{\sqrt{|I|}} \right\} \\
		& \hspace{5cm} \geq 	1 - c_1 (n \vee p)^{-288^2C_x^2d_0c_2/c_x^2} - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3},
	\end{align*}
	where $C_3 > 0$ is an absolute constant depending on all the other absolute constants, $c_1, c_2, c_3$ are absolute constants defined in Lemmas~\ref{lem-RE} and \ref{lem-x-bound}.
nodes.statement_short: On an interval without change points and long enough, the interval Lasso has $\ell_2$ error $\lesssim\lambda\sqrt{d_0/|I|}$ and $\ell_1$ error $\lesssim\lambda d_0/\sqrt{|I|}$ w.h.p.
assumptions: For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{a}) and (\textbf{c})
if there exists no true change point in $I = (s, e]$, with $|I| > 288^2 C^2_x d_0 \log(n \vee p)/c_x^2$
\lambda \geq \lambda_1 := C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{\log(n \vee p)},
nodes.label: lemma:lasso

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
Let $v = \widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_I$.  Since $|I| > \log(n \vee p)$, it follows from the definition of $\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I$ that
	\[
		\sum_{t \in I} (y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I)^2 + \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \leq \sum_{t \in I} (y_t - x_t^{\top}\beta^*_I)^2 + \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1,
	\]
	which leads to
	\begin{equation} \sum_{t \in I}(x_t^{\top}v)^2 + \lambda\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \leq \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1 + 2 \sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top}v \leq \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1 +  \frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|v\|_1,
	\end{equation}
	where the last inequality holds on the event $\mathcal{B}_I$, with the choice of $\lambda$ and due to \Cref{lem-x-bound}.  Note that
	\begin{equation} \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \geq \|\beta^*_I(S)\|_1 - \|v(S)\|_1 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1
	\end{equation}
	and 
	\begin{equation} \|v\|_1 = \|v(S)\|_1 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1.
	\end{equation}
	Combining \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-1}, \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-2} and \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-3} yields
	\begin{equation} \sum_{t \in I}(x_t^{\top}v)^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S)\|_1,
	\end{equation}
	which in turn implies
	\[
		\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 \leq 3\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S)\|_1.
	\]
	
On the event of $\mathcal{E}_I$, it holds that
	\begin{align}
		\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I} \bigl(x_t^{\top}v\bigr)^2} & \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v\|_1 \nonumber \\
		& = \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S)\|_1 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S^c)\|_1 \nonumber \\
		& \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 36 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S)\|_1 \geq  \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 36 C_x \sqrt{d_0 \log(p)}\|v(S)\|_2 \nonumber \\
		& \geq \left(\frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} - 36 C_x \sqrt{d_0 \log(p)}\right) \|v\|_2 > \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{8} \|v\|_2, \end{align}
	where the second inequality follows from \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-4}, the third inequality follows from \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{a}) and the last inequality follows from the choice of $|I|$.
	
Combining \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-4} and \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-5} leads to
	\[
		\frac{c_x^2|I|}{64} \|v\|_2^2 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|} \|v(S)\|_1 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|d_0} \|v\|_2,
	\]	
	therefore
	\[
		\|v\|_2 \leq \frac{96 \lambda\sqrt{d_0}}{\sqrt{|I|} c_x^2}
	\]
	and 
	\[
		\|v\|_1 = \|v(S)\|_1 + \|v(S^c)\|_1 \leq 4\|v(S)\|_1 \leq 4\sqrt{d_0}\|v\|_2 \leq \frac{384 \lambda d_0}{\sqrt{|I|} c_x^2}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Standard Lasso argument: basic inequality on the noise event gives the cone condition, then the restricted eigenvalue event bounds $\|v\|_2$ and $\|v\|_1$.

nodes.name: Basic inequality
nodes.statement: \sum_{t \in I}(x_t^{\top}v)^2 + \lambda\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \leq \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1 + 2 \sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top}v \leq \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1 +  \frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|v\|_1,
nodes.label: eq-lem9-pf-1

nodes.name: l1 norm lower bound
nodes.statement: \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \geq \|\beta^*_I(S)\|_1 - \|v(S)\|_1 + \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1
nodes.label: eq-lem9-pf-2

nodes.name: Cone condition
nodes.statement: \sum_{t \in I}(x_t^{\top}v)^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S)\|_1,
nodes.label: eq-lem9-pf-4

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalue bound
nodes.statement:
\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I} \bigl(x_t^{\top}v\bigr)^2} & \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v\|_1 \nonumber \\
		& = \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S)\|_1 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S^c)\|_1 \nonumber \\
		& \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 36 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S)\|_1 \geq  \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 36 C_x \sqrt{d_0 \log(p)}\|v(S)\|_2 \nonumber \\
		& \geq \left(\frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} - 36 C_x \sqrt{d_0 \log(p)}\right) \|v\|_2 > \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{8} \|v\|_2,
nodes.label: eq-lem9-pf-5

nodes.name: Basic inequality
nodes.statement:
Let $v = \widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I - \beta^*_I$.  Since $|I| > \log(n \vee p)$, it follows from the definition of $\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I$ that
	\[
		\sum_{t \in I} (y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I)^2 + \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \leq \sum_{t \in I} (y_t - x_t^{\top}\beta^*_I)^2 + \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1,
	\]
	which leads to
	\begin{equation} \sum_{t \in I}(x_t^{\top}v)^2 + \lambda\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I\|_1 \leq \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1 + 2 \sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top}v \leq \lambda \sqrt{|I|}\|\beta^*_I\|_1 +  \frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|v\|_1,
	\end{equation}
	where the last inequality holds on the event $\mathcal{B}_I$, with the choice of $\lambda$ and due to \Cref{lem-x-bound}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the Lasso objective at $\widehat\beta$ and $\beta^*_I$; bound the noise term on $\mathcal{B}_I$.

nodes.name: Norm decompositions
nodes.statement_short: Split $\ell_1$ norms over $S$ and $S^c$.

nodes.name: Cone condition
nodes.statement:
Combining \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-1}, \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-2} and \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-3} yields
	\begin{equation} \sum_{t \in I}(x_t^{\top}v)^2 + \frac{\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|}\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S)\|_1,
	\end{equation}
	which in turn implies
	\[
		\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 \leq 3\|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S)\|_1.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Derive the cone condition $\|\widehat\beta(S^c)\|_1 \le 3\|\widehat\beta(S)\|_1$.

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalue
nodes.statement:
On the event of $\mathcal{E}_I$, it holds that
	\begin{align}
		\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I} \bigl(x_t^{\top}v\bigr)^2} & \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v\|_1 \nonumber \\
		& = \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S)\|_1 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S^c)\|_1 \nonumber \\
		& \geq \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 36 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|v(S)\|_1 \geq  \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} \|v\|_2 - 36 C_x \sqrt{d_0 \log(p)}\|v(S)\|_2 \nonumber \\
		& \geq \left(\frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{4} - 36 C_x \sqrt{d_0 \log(p)}\right) \|v\|_2 > \frac{c_x\sqrt{|I|}}{8} \|v\|_2, \end{align}
	where the second inequality follows from \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-4}, the third inequality follows from \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}(\textbf{a}) and the last inequality follows from the choice of $|I|$.
nodes.statement_short: On $\mathcal{E}_I$, the prediction norm dominates $c_x\sqrt{|I|}\|v\|_2/8$.

nodes.name: Conclude error bounds
nodes.statement:
Combining \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-4} and \eqref{eq-lem9-pf-5} leads to
	\[
		\frac{c_x^2|I|}{64} \|v\|_2^2 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|} \|v(S)\|_1 \leq \frac{3\lambda}{2}\sqrt{|I|d_0} \|v\|_2,
	\]	
	therefore
	\[
		\|v\|_2 \leq \frac{96 \lambda\sqrt{d_0}}{\sqrt{|I|} c_x^2}
	\]
	and 
	\[
		\|v\|_1 = \|v(S)\|_1 + \|v(S^c)\|_1 \leq 4\|v(S)\|_1 \leq 4\sqrt{d_0}\|v\|_2 \leq \frac{384 \lambda d_0}{\sqrt{|I|} c_x^2}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound $\|v\|_2$ and $\|v\|_1$.

nodes.statement_short: On a change-free interval, the RSS of the interval Lasso differs from that of the truth by at most $\lambda^2 d_0$ (long intervals) or $C_4\lambda\sqrt{\log(n\vee p)}d_0^{3/2}$ (short ones) w.h.p.

conclusions:
\mathbb{P}\left\{\left|\sum_{t \in I} \bigl\{(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta})^2 - (y_t - x_t^{\top}\beta^*)^2\bigr\}\right| \leq \lambda^2 d_0 \right\} \\
		& \hspace{2cm}\geq 	1 - c_1 (n \vee p)^{-288^2C_x^2d_0c_2/c_x^2} - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3};

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 10

nodes.name: Notation

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 11
nodes.statement_short: Basic inequality with an extra bias term from varying coefficients, bounded by sub-exponential concentration; then argue as in Lemma 9.

nodes.name: Basic inequality with bias term
nodes.statement:
& \sum_{t \in I} \bigl\{x_t^{\top}(\widehat{\beta} - \beta^*)\bigr\}^2 + 2(\widehat{\beta} - \beta^*)^{\top}\sum_{t \in I} x_t x_t^{\top}(\beta^* - \beta^*_t) \nonumber \\
		& \hspace{3cm} \leq 2\sum_{t \in I} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top}(\widehat{\beta} - \beta^*) + \lambda \sqrt{\max\{|I|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}}\bigl(\bigl\|\beta^*\bigr\|_1 - \bigl\|\widehat{\beta}\bigr\|_1\bigr).
nodes.label: eq-lem10-pf-2

nodes.name: Bias term deviation bound
nodes.statement:
\left\|\sum_{t \in I} x_t x_t^\top (\beta^*  -\beta^*_t) \right\|_{\infty} \leq 2C_x C_{\beta}\sqrt{d_0}\max\{\sqrt{|I|\log(n \vee p)}, \, \log(n \vee p)\}\nonumber \\
		\leq \lambda \sqrt{\max\{|I|, \, \log(n \vee p)\}}/4.
nodes.label: eq-lem10-pf-1

nodes.name: Basic inequality
nodes.statement_short: Compare objectives at $\widehat\beta$ and the averaged coefficient.

nodes.name: Bias term has mean zero
nodes.statement:
We bound	
	\[
		\left\|\sum_{t \in I} x_t x_t^\top (\beta^*  -\beta^*_t) \right\|_{\infty}.  
	\]
	For any $k \in \{1, \ldots, p\}$, the $k$th entry of $\sum_{t \in I} x_t x_t^\top (\beta^*  -\beta^*_t)$ satisfies that
	\begin{align*}
		& \mathbb{E}\left\{\sum_{t \in I} \sum_{j = 1}^p x_t(k)x_t(j)(\beta^*(j) - \beta^*_t(j))\right\} = \sum_{t \in I}\sum_{j = 1}^p \mathbb{E}\{x_t(k) x_t(j)\}\{\beta^*(j) - \beta^*_t(j)\} \\
		= & \sum_{j = 1}^p \mathbb{E}\{x_1(k) x_1(j)\} \sum_{t \in I}\{\beta^*(j) - \beta^*_t(j)\} = 0.
	\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The cross term with $\beta^*-\beta^*_t$ has zero mean.

nodes.name: Concentration of the bias term
nodes.statement_short: Sub-exponential concentration bounds the bias term by $\lambda\sqrt{\max\{|I|,\log\}}/4$.

nodes.name: Combine on noise event
nodes.statement_short: On $\mathcal{B}_I$ combine the bounds.

nodes.name: Conclude as in Lemma 9
nodes.statement: The final claims follow from the same arguments as in \Cref{lemma:lasso}.
nodes.statement_short: Finish with the argument of Lemma 9.

nodes.name: Case (i): one change point in a DP interval
nodes.statement:
With the conditions and notation in \Cref{proposition:dp step 1}, assume that $I = (s, e] \in \widehat{\mathcal{P}}$ has one and only one true change point $\eta$.  Denote $I_1 = (s, \eta]$, $I_2 = (\eta, e]$ and $\|\beta_{I_1}^* - \beta_{I_2}^*\|_2 = \kappa$.  If, in addition, it holds that  
	\begin{align} \sum_{t \in I}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_I)^2 \leq \sum_{t \in I_1}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I_1})^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I_2})^2 + \gamma,
	\end{align}
	then with 
	\[
		\lambda \geq \lambda_2 = C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{d_0 \log(n \vee p)}, 
	\]
	where $C_{\lambda} > 8C_{\beta}C_x/\sigma_{\varepsilon}$, it holds with probability at least $1 - 2c_1 (n \vee p)^{-288^2C_x^2d_0c_2/c_x^2} - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3}$ that, that
	\[
		\min\{|I_1 |,\, |I_2|\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right).
	\]
nodes.statement_short: If a DP interval with exactly one change point is not split, one of its two pieces has length at most $C_\epsilon(\lambda^2 d_0+\gamma)/\kappa^2$.

nodes.statement: \sum_{t \in I}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_I)^2 \leq \sum_{t \in I_1}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I_1})^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I_2})^2 + \gamma,
nodes.label: eq:one change point

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 12
nodes.statement:
First we notice that with the choice of $\lambda$, it holds that 
	\[
		\lambda \geq \max\{\lambda_1, \, \lambda_2\},
	\]
	and therefore we can apply Lemmas~\ref{lemma:lasso}, \ref{lemma:RSS lasso} and \ref{lemma:oracle 2} when needed.

We prove by contradiction, assuming that
	\begin{equation} \min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\} > C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right) > 288^2 C^2_x d_0 \log(n \vee p)/c_x^2,
	\end{equation}
	where the second inequality follows from the observation that $\kappa^2 \leq 4 d_0 C^2_{\beta}$.  Therefore we also have
	\[
		\min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\} > \log(n \vee p).
	\]

It follows from \Cref{lemma:RSS lasso} and \eqref{eq:one change point} that, with probability at least $1 - 2c_1 (n \vee p)^{-288^2C_x^2d_0c_2/c_x^2} - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3}$ that, that
	\begin{align}
		& \sum_{t \in I_1}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_I)^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_I)^2 = \sum_{ t\in I}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_I)^2  \nonumber \\
		\leq & \sum_{t \in I_1}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I_1})^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I_2})^2 + \gamma \nonumber \\
		\leq & \sum_{t \in I_1}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\beta^*_{I_1})^2 + \sum_{t \in I_2}(y_t - x_t^{\top}\beta^*_{I_2})^2 + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0. \end{align}

Denoting $\Delta_i = \widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I} - \beta_{I_i}^*$, $i = 1, 2$, \eqref{eq-lem-1cp-pf-1} leads to that  
	\begin{align}
		& \sum_{t\in I_1} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_1)^2 + \sum_{t\in I _2 } (x_t^{\top}\Delta_2)^2 \leq 2\sum_{t\in I_1} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top} \Delta_1 + 2\sum_{t\in I_2} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top} \Delta_2  + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		\leq & 2 \left\|\sum_{t\in I_1} \varepsilon_t x_t  \right\|_{\infty} \|\Delta_1\|_1 + 2 \left\|\sum_{t\in I_2} \varepsilon_t x_t  \right\|_{\infty} \|\Delta_2\|_1 + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		\leq & 2 \left\|\sum_{t\in I_1} \varepsilon_t x_t  \right\|_{\infty} \bigl(\|\Delta_1(S)\|_1 + \|\Delta_1(S^c)\|_1\bigr) + 2 \left\|\sum_{t\in I_2} \varepsilon_t x_t  \right\|_{\infty} \bigl(\|\Delta_2(S)\|_1 + \|\Delta_2(S^c)\|_1\bigr) \nonumber \\
		& \hspace{5cm} + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		\leq & 2 \left\|\sum_{t\in I_1} \varepsilon_t x_t  \right\|_{\infty} \bigl(\sqrt{d_0}\|\Delta_1(S)\|_2 + \|\Delta_1(S^c)\|_1\bigr) + 2 \left\|\sum_{t\in I_2} \varepsilon_t x_t  \right\|_{\infty} \bigl(\sqrt{d_0}\|\Delta_2(S)\|_2 + \|\Delta_2(S^c)\|_1\bigr) \nonumber \\
		& \hspace{5cm} + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0. \end{align}
	
On the events $\mathcal{B}_{I_1} \cap \mathcal{B}_{I_2}$, it holds that
	\begin{align}
		\eqref{eq:one change point first step} & \leq \lambda/2 \big(\sqrt{|I_1|d_0}\|\Delta_1(S)\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\Delta_1(S^c)\|_1 + \sqrt{|I_2|d_0} \|\Delta_2(S)\|_2 \nonumber \\
		& \hspace{1cm} + \sqrt{|I_2|}\|\Delta_2(S^c)\|_1\big) + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		& \leq \frac{32 \lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{\lambda (\sqrt{|I_1|} + \sqrt{|I_2|})}{2} \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		& \leq \frac{32 \lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2}{256} + \gamma + 4C_3 \lambda^2 d_0, \end{align}
	where the second inequality follows from $2ab \leq a^2 + b^2$, letting
	\[
		a = 4\lambda \sqrt{d_0}/c_x \quad \mbox{and} \quad b = c_x \sqrt{|I_j|}\|\Delta_1\|_2/16, \quad j = 1, 2,
	\]
	and the last inequality follows from \Cref{lemma:oracle 2}.

\vskip 3mm
Note that 
	\begin{align*}
		\|\Delta_1\|_1 \leq \|\Delta_1(S)\|_1 + \|\Delta_1(S^c)\|_1 \leq \sqrt{d_0}\|\Delta_1\|_2 + \frac{C_5 \lambda d_0 }{\sqrt{|I_1|}},
	\end{align*}
	which combines with \eqref{eq-contra}, on the event $\mathcal{E}_{I_1}$, leads to
	\[
		\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I_1} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_1)^2} > \frac{c_x \sqrt{|I_1|}}{4} \|\Delta_1\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|\Delta_1\|_1 > \frac{c_x \sqrt{|I_1|}}{8} \|\Delta_1\|_2 - \frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_1|}}.
	\]

Moreover, we have
	\begin{align}
		& \sqrt{|I_1|} \|\Delta_1\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_2|} \|\Delta_2\|_2 \geq \sqrt{|I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2 + |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2} \nonumber \\
		\geq & \sqrt{\inf_{v \in \mathbb{R}^p} \{|I_1| \|\beta^*_{\eta} - v\|^2 + |I_2| \|\beta^*_{\eta + 1} - v\|^2\}} = \kappa \sqrt{\frac{|I_1||I_2|}{|I|}} \geq \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{2}}\min\{\sqrt{|I_1|}, \sqrt{|I_2|} \}. \end{align}
	
Therefore, on the event $\mathcal{E}_{I_1} \cap \mathcal{E}_{I_2} \cap \mathcal{B}_{I_1} \cap \mathcal{B}_{I_2}$, combining \eqref{eq:one change point first step} and \eqref{eq-upper-long},  we have that
	\begin{align*}
		&  \sqrt{|I_1|} \|\Delta_1\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_2|} \|\Delta_2\|_2 \leq \frac{8}{c_x} \left(\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I_1} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_1)^2} + \sqrt{\sum_{t \in I_2} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_2)^2} \right) \\
		& \hspace{5cm} + \frac{8}{c_x}\left(\frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_1|}} + \frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_2|}}\right) \\
		& \leq \frac{8\sqrt{2}}{c_x} \sqrt{\frac{32 \lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2}{256} + \gamma + 4C_3 \lambda^2 d_0} \\
		& \hspace{5cm} + \frac{8}{c_x}\left(\frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_1|}} + \frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_2|}}\right)  \\
		& \leq \frac{64\lambda \sqrt{d_0}}{c_x^2} + \frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\Delta_1\|_2}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{|I_2|}\|\Delta_2\|_2}{2} + 	\frac{8\sqrt{2\gamma}}{c_x}	+ \frac{16\sqrt{2C_3} \lambda \sqrt{d_0}}{c_x} + \frac{C_5\lambda \sqrt{d_0}}{2c_x^2},
	\end{align*}
	which implies that
	\begin{align} \frac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{2} \left(\sqrt{|I_1|} \|\Delta_1\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_2|} \|\Delta_2\|_2 \right) \leq \frac{128 + 32\sqrt{2}c_x\sqrt{C_3} + C_5}{2c_x^2} \lambda\sqrt{d_0} + 	\frac{8\sqrt{2\gamma}}{c_x}.
	\end{align}
	Combining \eqref{eq-lower-long} and \eqref{eq-2-sqrt-2} yields
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}\kappa \sqrt{\min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\}} \leq \frac{128 + 32\sqrt{2}c_x\sqrt{C_3} + C_5}{2c_x^2} \lambda\sqrt{d_0} + 	\frac{8\sqrt{2\gamma}}{c_x},	 
	\end{align*}
	therefore
	\[
		\min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right),
	\]
	which is a contradiction with \eqref{eq-contra}.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: if both pieces are long, oracle bounds on the common Lasso fit contradict the $\kappa\sqrt{|I_1||I_2|/|I|}$ lower bound.

nodes.statement: \min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\} > C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right) > 288^2 C^2_x d_0 \log(n \vee p)/c_x^2,

	\]

We prove by contradiction, assuming that
	\begin{equation} \min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\} > C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right) > 288^2 C^2_x d_0 \log(n \vee p)/c_x^2,

Denoting $\Delta_i = \widehat{\beta}^\lambda_{I} - \beta_{I_i}^*$, $i = 1, 2$, \eqref{eq-lem-1cp-pf-1} leads to that  
	\begin{align}
		& \sum_{t\in I_1} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_1)^2 + \sum_{t\in I _2 } (x_t^{\top}\Delta_2)^2 \leq 2\sum_{t\in I_1} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top} \Delta_1 + 2\sum_{t\in I_2} \varepsilon_t x_t^{\top} \Delta_2  + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\

		& \hspace{5cm} + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand to bound prediction errors by noise cross terms.

nodes.name: Upper bound on noise events
nodes.statement:
On the events $\mathcal{B}_{I_1} \cap \mathcal{B}_{I_2}$, it holds that
	\begin{align}
		\eqref{eq:one change point first step} & \leq \lambda/2 \big(\sqrt{|I_1|d_0}\|\Delta_1(S)\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\Delta_1(S^c)\|_1 + \sqrt{|I_2|d_0} \|\Delta_2(S)\|_2 \nonumber \\
		& \hspace{1cm} + \sqrt{|I_2|}\|\Delta_2(S^c)\|_1\big) + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		& \leq \frac{32 \lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{\lambda (\sqrt{|I_1|} + \sqrt{|I_2|})}{2} \|\widehat{\beta}^{\lambda}_I(S^c)\|_1 + \gamma + 2C_3 \lambda^2 d_0 \nonumber \\
		& \leq \frac{32 \lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2}{256} + \gamma + 4C_3 \lambda^2 d_0, \end{align}
	where the second inequality follows from $2ab \leq a^2 + b^2$, letting
	\[
		a = 4\lambda \sqrt{d_0}/c_x \quad \mbox{and} \quad b = c_x \sqrt{|I_j|}\|\Delta_1\|_2/16, \quad j = 1, 2,
	\]
	and the last inequality follows from \Cref{lemma:oracle 2}.
nodes.statement_short: On the noise events, bound by $\lambda^2 d_0$, $\gamma$ and small multiples of the errors.

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalue lower bound
nodes.statement:
Note that 
	\begin{align*}
		\|\Delta_1\|_1 \leq \|\Delta_1(S)\|_1 + \|\Delta_1(S^c)\|_1 \leq \sqrt{d_0}\|\Delta_1\|_2 + \frac{C_5 \lambda d_0 }{\sqrt{|I_1|}},
	\end{align*}
	which combines with \eqref{eq-contra}, on the event $\mathcal{E}_{I_1}$, leads to
	\[
		\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I_1} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_1)^2} > \frac{c_x \sqrt{|I_1|}}{4} \|\Delta_1\|_2 - 9 C_x \sqrt{\log(p)}\|\Delta_1\|_1 > \frac{c_x \sqrt{|I_1|}}{8} \|\Delta_1\|_2 - \frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_1|}}.
	\]
nodes.statement_short: On $\mathcal{E}_{I_1}$ lower-bound the prediction error.

nodes.name: Jump size lower bound
nodes.statement_short: Errors are at least $\kappa\min\{\sqrt{|I_1|},\sqrt{|I_2|}\}/\sqrt 2$.

nodes.name: Combine bounds
nodes.statement:
Therefore, on the event $\mathcal{E}_{I_1} \cap \mathcal{E}_{I_2} \cap \mathcal{B}_{I_1} \cap \mathcal{B}_{I_2}$, combining \eqref{eq:one change point first step} and \eqref{eq-upper-long},  we have that
	\begin{align*}
		&  \sqrt{|I_1|} \|\Delta_1\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_2|} \|\Delta_2\|_2 \leq \frac{8}{c_x} \left(\sqrt{\sum_{t \in I_1} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_1)^2} + \sqrt{\sum_{t \in I_2} (x_t^{\top}\Delta_2)^2} \right) \\
		& \hspace{5cm} + \frac{8}{c_x}\left(\frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_1|}} + \frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_2|}}\right) \\
		& \leq \frac{8\sqrt{2}}{c_x} \sqrt{\frac{32 \lambda^2 d_0}{c_x^2} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_1| \|\Delta_1\|_2^2}{256} + \frac{c_x^2 |I_2| \|\Delta_2\|_2^2}{256} + \gamma + 4C_3 \lambda^2 d_0} \\
		& \hspace{5cm} + \frac{8}{c_x}\left(\frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_1|}} + \frac{9C_5 C_x\lambda d_0 \sqrt{\log(p)} }{c_x^2 \sqrt{|I_2|}}\right)  \\
		& \leq \frac{64\lambda \sqrt{d_0}}{c_x^2} + \frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{|I_1|}\|\Delta_1\|_2}{2} + \frac{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{|I_2|}\|\Delta_2\|_2}{2} + 	\frac{8\sqrt{2\gamma}}{c_x}	+ \frac{16\sqrt{2C_3} \lambda \sqrt{d_0}}{c_x} + \frac{C_5\lambda \sqrt{d_0}}{2c_x^2},
	\end{align*}
	which implies that
	\begin{align} \frac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{2} \left(\sqrt{|I_1|} \|\Delta_1\|_2 + \sqrt{|I_2|} \|\Delta_2\|_2 \right) \leq \frac{128 + 32\sqrt{2}c_x\sqrt{C_3} + C_5}{2c_x^2} \lambda\sqrt{d_0} + 	\frac{8\sqrt{2\gamma}}{c_x}.
	\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Combine upper and lower bounds.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement:
Combining \eqref{eq-lower-long} and \eqref{eq-2-sqrt-2} yields
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}\kappa \sqrt{\min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\}} \leq \frac{128 + 32\sqrt{2}c_x\sqrt{C_3} + C_5}{2c_x^2} \lambda\sqrt{d_0} + 	\frac{8\sqrt{2\gamma}}{c_x},	 
	\end{align*}
	therefore
	\[
		\min\{|I_1|, \, |I_2|\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right),
	\]
	which is a contradiction with \eqref{eq-contra}.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the claimed bound, contradicting the hypothesis.

nodes.name: Case (ii): two change points in a DP interval
nodes.statement:
For \Cref{assume:change point regression model}, under \Cref{assume:high dim coefficient}, with 
	\[
		\lambda \geq \lambda_2 = C_{\lambda}\sigma_{\varepsilon} \sqrt{d_0 \log(n \vee p)}, 
	\]
	where $C_{\lambda} > 8C_{\beta}C_x/\sigma_{\varepsilon}$, $I = (s, e]$ containing exactly two change points $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$.  Denote $ I_1 =(s,\eta_1] $, $I_2 = (\eta_1,\eta_2] $, $I_3 =(\eta_2,e]$, $\|  \beta_{I_1} ^*  -\beta_{I_2} ^* \|_2 = \kappa_1$ and $\|  \beta_{I_2} ^*  -\beta_{I_3} ^* \|_2 = \kappa_2$.  If in addition it holds that  
	\[
		 \sum_{t\in I } (y_t -x_t^{\top} \widehat \beta^\lambda_ I )^2 \leq \sum_{t\in I_1 } (y_t -x_t^{\top} \widehat \beta^\lambda_ {I_1}  )^2 + \sum_{t\in I_2 } (y_t -x_t^{\top} \widehat \beta^\lambda_ {I_2}  )^2  + \sum_{t\in I_3} (y_t -x_t^{\top} \widehat \beta^\lambda_ {I_3}  )^2 + 2\gamma, 
	\]
	then 
	\begin{align*}
		\max\{|I_1|, \, |I_3|\} \leq C_{\epsilon} \left(\frac{\lambda^2 d_0 + \gamma}{\kappa^2}\right),
	\end{align*} 
	with probability at least $1 - 3c_1 (n \vee p)^{-288^2C_x^2d_0c_2/c_x^2} - 2(n \vee p)^{-c_3}$.
nodes.statement_short: If a DP interval with exactly two change points is not split, its outer pieces have length at most $C_\epsilon(\lambda^2 d_0+\gamma)/\kappa^2$.
